perplexity.description:
The 1985 album Music From The Motion Picture Soundtrack "Fletch" by Various Artists is a vibrant collection that blends electronic, pop, and film score elements, capturing the playful and irreverent spirit of the cult comedy. Released by MCA Records, the soundtrack features a mix of original songs and instrumental cues, anchored by Harold Faltermeyer’s sleek synth-driven themes, which showcase his signature 1980s electronic style. The album also includes pop tracks from artists like Stephanie Mills, Dan Hartman, The Fixx, and Kim Wilde, whose contributions add a contemporary pop and new wave flavor to the mix. Faltermeyer’s “Fletch Theme” stands out as a highlight, echoing the digital energy of his earlier work on Beverly Hills Cop.

This soundtrack holds a notable place in Faltermeyer’s discography as one of his most recognizable film scores, further cementing his reputation as a leading composer of 1980s electronic film music. While the album did not achieve major chart success, it became a cult favorite among fans of the era’s synth-pop and movie soundtracks. Critics praised its energetic and stylish production, with the blend of pop songs and electronic instrumentals reflecting the film’s comedic tone and Chevy Chase’s charismatic performance. The album remains a quintessential example of 1980s film music, celebrated for its catchy melodies and distinctive electronic sound.
